chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Meeting Fats Navarro in Kirk's band
summary: Back with Kirk in Cincinnati, McGhee hears a beautiful trumpet from the ballroom; it is Fats Navarro, with Big Jim Lawson also in the section.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: And when I went back with the band, something funny happened. I don't know what it was. I can't remember what the hell it was. But I didn't stay too long anyway after that. I didn't stay too long there. I remember I went back with Kirk, because that's when I met Fat Girl, heh-heh...
When was this? '44?
'43, I think.
Still '43?
'43, yeah.
And you met Fats.
Yeah, yeah. Boy, that was somethin'. Oh, I
heard this cat from downstairs after I was getting out of the cab... I heard him playing, I said, 'Now, who is that? I know that ain't nobody I know.' And I went upstairs, and he...
Where was this? In the hotel?
No, this was in the ballroom.
Oh, in the ballroom.
They were in the ballroom playing. This was in Cincinnati. So I joined the band... I came to join the band, and I got out of the cab, and I heard...
Now, this is the time between the two Barnet stints.
Yeah.
Okay, so you were with Kirk.

This is when I went back with Kirk. And I hear this big sound coming, floating out of the ballroom. And I said, 'Who in the hell is that?' I'm so amazed that Andy would have a trumpet player that played that pretty, because he thought Big Jim was the greatest thing that God ever created, and Big Jim was just a big, loud-playin' trumpet player...
Big Jim Lawson.
Yeah. He was a good lead man, but I said if you put him on the fourth part, he sounded like he was playin' lead anyway. Ha-ha-ha!
He didn't know how to tone it down.
Yeah, man. Well, he couldn't tone it down. He couldn't do that.
So that's where you met Fats Navarro, huh?
Yeah. We're going to have to let this go for the time being...
[PAUSE]
